lines.meet: I'm Alonso, and I do fire. Stand a bit further back than you'd think, mijo, and you'll keep your eyebrows.
lines.meet_neighbour: You live out in the ruins too, no? I'm Alonso, with the fire-pit. Come by when the kiln's cooling and I'll make coffee.
lines.ask_home: Where's home for you, mijo? Where you're from, I mean, not where you sleep.
lines.ask_work: What did your hands do before all this? You can tell a lot about a person from that.
lines.answer_home: Puebla, in Mexico, where the blue and white pottery comes from. Every church in the city has our tiles on it somewhere.
lines.answer_work: I was a potter, the third in my family to run the kiln. Twenty-two years of four hours of heat that had to go exactly right.
lines.chat_food: I'd ask for mole on a Sunday, my mother-in-law's recipe. It's got twenty-six things in it and it takes three days.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep beside the fire-pit, because a kiln cooling down is the best sound in the world. It ticks all night like a big slow clock.
lines.chat_missing: My sons used to come home on Sundays and complain about Mexico City. I'd give them a plate and let them talk.
lines.chat_here: This world's one big kiln with a strange character, mijo. You learn where it runs hot and you don't stand there.
lines.tease_quiet: {name}, you're so quiet I keep checking you're still behind me. Make a little noise so I don't set you on fire by accident.
lines.tease_talker: Órale, {name}, you've told that story three times and it gets longer every time. By Friday it'll take a whole firing.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, you're nearly as careful as I am, and I'm a man who's actually been on fire.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, I've seen you run into worse than my kiln and come out laughing. Your eyebrows are braver than mine.
lines.tease_any: Ay, {name}, if you were a pot I'd keep you, even with the crack. The good ones always have one somewhere.
lines.tease_back: Mijo, my own sons have teased me for twenty years, and they're much better at it than you. Have another go.
lines.take_it_kindly: Ha, that's fair, {name}. My wife used to say the same thing, only louder.
lines.bristle: Leave that one alone, {name}. Tease me about anything else, but not that.
lines.apologise: Perdón, that came out wrong. I'm sorry, I didn't mean it the way it sounded.
lines.double_down: No, I'll stand by it. Somebody has to say it, and I'm old enough not to care.
lines.needle_quiet: You don't say a word, and then you're standing right in my heat. Tell me where you are, please.
lines.needle_talker: You talk the whole way, and I can't hear the fire. In my trade that's how people lose their hands.
lines.needle_careful: You check everything twice and you still stand right where my fire goes. Watch my hands, not the door.
lines.needle_bold: You run at everything like heat's a joke. I've seen what it does to people, and it's never funny afterwards.
lines.needle_any: You're careless around my fire, and I've told you before. I'm tired of telling you.
lines.bite_back: Mijo, I've fired a kiln for twenty-two years without hurting anybody. Don't you tell me about being careless.
lines.hurt: Okay, mijo, I heard you. Let's leave it there for now.
lines.laugh_off: Ay, you sound like my father. He shouted at me for thirty years and I'm still here.
lines.confide: {name}, my wife Lupe sold our pots at the market in Puebla. She was there when it happened. I don't talk about it with many people.
lines.listen: Thank you, {name}. Sit here by the fire with me a while, and we don't have to say anything else.
lines.look_out: {name}, stay on this side of me when I start. The heat goes left, always, and I want you out of it.
lines.accept: Okay, {name}, I'll listen to you this once. Don't tell anybody, it's bad for my reputation.
lines.deflect: Ay, I'm fine, {name}. I've had worse burns from my own coffee.
lines.check_in: {name}, anything burned? Show me your hands, and then your face.
lines.blame: That fire went where it shouldn't have, and it wasn't mine. I'd like to know whose it was.
lines.thank: You pulled me out of that one, and I felt it go. Gracias, from the bottom of my heart.
lines.brush_off: Ah, it's nothing, it's what we do. Sit down before you fall down.
lines.worry: {name}, you scared me half to death. I'm making coffee, and you're drinking it.
lines.handed_down: This was yours, no? I'll take good care of it, I promise you.
lines.hand_fine: Keep it, mijo, it suits you better. I've got my goggles, and that's all I need.
lines.hand_sulk: That was mine, and nobody asked me. I'll get over it, but not today.
lines.turn_friendly: You know, {name}, I like having you around. You don't flinch when I light up, and that's rare.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, you're family now. I'd let you watch me fire a kiln, and I don't let anybody watch.
lines.turn_grating: We rub each other the wrong way, you and me. It happens, and we'll work around it.
lines.turn_rivals: Stay out of my heat and I'll stay out of your way. That's the best I can offer.
lines.make_up: {name}, I've been an old fool with you. Come and have coffee, and we'll start over.
lines.defend: Hey, leave {name} alone. I was watching, and that wasn't anybody's fault.
lines.friend_left: {name}'s gone home for a bit. The fire's no fun without somebody to joke with while it burns.
lines.friend_back: {name}, you're back! And you've still got both eyebrows, I see.
lines.common_spanish: Ay, it's good to hear somebody speak properly. My English gets tired by the end of the day.
lines.common_mexico: You're Mexican too? Qué padre, tell me where you're from, and I'll guess what your mother cooked on Sundays.
lines.common_parent: I've got two sons, both grown, both in Mexico City. Neither of them wanted the kiln, and I minded more than I let them see.
lines.common_craft: Twenty-two years at a kiln taught me that good work takes as long as it takes. You work with your hands too, I can see it.
